grid.note: First-world Eris workspace origin from the $7A92/$7A2C world-local camera pairs; 65,536 raw units per cell (docs/research/damocles-catalogue.md).

start.evidence: research/damocles-st/snapshots/eris-spaceport-onfoot.sav: $7A92 = $004770B1, $7A96 = 63, $7A9A = $00886C2D, on foot ($7A8E = 1), cell $87; camera yaw word $7AA2 = $0600, the panel compass centred on N (docs/research/damocles-walk-board-flight.md, yaw-probe runs 2026-09-11).

walk.evidence: Speed: 3 cells over 30,000 VBL at 50 Hz (observe-walk-toward-building run, docs/research/damocles-walk-board-flight.md); one observation, no step model (#205). Turn: $7AA2 advances $50 yaw units in the first second of a held stick (80/1024 of a turn, 0.49 rad/s) and quickens to about $70 per second after four seconds; the constant here is the opening rate and the acceleration is not modelled (#205).

orientation.note: Camera yaw $7AA2 (twin $7AC2) wraps every 1024 units; N is centred at $0200 mod $0400, E at $0300, S at $0000, W at $0100, and a right stick raises it. Walking at N raises $7A9A (z) and at E raises $7A92 (x), so Eris is left-handed seen from above with +y up; the frame mirrors z for the shared right-handed Camera. Instance heading bytes at $79CD+slot are 256 steps per turn on the same clockwise sense with zero at north (camera ≡ byte×4+$200 mod $400). Whether a model's z runs with world z is not decoded; modelZ is authored to match the Working Authority's spaceport view (docs/research/damocles-walk-board-flight.md).

palette.note: Live hardware palette at $06FD00 while outdoors on foot (docs/research/damocles-filled-polygons.md).

ground.note: Authored cell-sized fill at y = 0 in the recovered green, only for cells whose catalogue ground record has no faces; extentCells is the Chebyshev neighbourhood of that fill (#221). Recovered pad and road polygons come from the Damocles Catalogue ground family (docs/research/damocles-eris-ground.md).

sky.note: Palette entry 246 read as the daytime sky; no sky model is decoded.

lighting.note: Reserved for an Enhanced-preset shadow pass (#209). Faces are drawn flat in their catalogue colours.
